entry_point: library API: compiling Snowflake SQL constructs with the dialect (COPY INTO / stage / file-format / MERGE command builders, custom table options, identifiers and labels)
scope_note: The advisory bundles two protections. This task builds only the code-generation half (CWE-89 identifier/literal injection while rendering SQL). The connection-URL / connector-kwarg half (CWE-73) is a different property over a different data path: not tested, not built on.

verified.entry_point: Every security test builds a public construct of snowflake.sqlalchemy and compiles it with the project's own entry point: `construct.compile(dialect=dialect(), compile_kwargs={'literal_binds': True, 'deterministic': True})` (the project's sql_compiler fixture). No server, network, GPU or GUI is involved.

routes: All identifier and literal sinks above were reproduced as emitting raw caller text on the shipped (pinned + injected) tree, and as inert on the oracle tree, offline.

COPY INTO from a Table renders copy_into.from_.name raw at the pinned commit and in current upstream (verified at origin/main 223f9d6: base.py:1076 `from_ = copy_into.from_.name`); pattern B, not touched by any published fix commit.

COPY INTO from a stage renders external_stage.namespace + name raw at the pinned commit and the published fix quotes only the file_format; current upstream later quotes the prefix (origin/main), so the route is present at the pinned commit but was fixed separately afterwards.

Considered and not tested: copy_options PATTERN / string partition_by / copy-option keys (documented raw-SQL surfaces), COPY INTO formatter non-string str(v) branch (not caller text), handle_cluster_by (denormalize_column_name already quotes unsafe values), Table/column comments (SQLAlchemy's literal processor escapes them), TargetLagOption (integer), KeywordOption (closed enum).
Out of scope, not tested: every connection-URL / connector-kwarg route in the other half of the advisory (snowdialect.create_connect_args, util._url, connect(), create_snowflake_engine).

wrong_fix_catalogue.refuse_all: n/a: there is no authorization decision; the refusal contract accepts a compile error for an unencodable value, and a fix that refuses everything (including legal values) is the over-broad functional failure, covered by ff_overquote.patch.
wrong_fix_catalogue.crash_as_refusal: n/a: nothing is refused at run time; the contract explicitly allows a compile-time error as the refusal form, so a crash on a hostile value is indistinguishable from a refusal and is not a failure mode this task scores.
wrong_fix_catalogue.wrong_resource: n/a: no authority or proxy object; every renderer encodes the exact value it is about to place in the statement.
wrong_fix_catalogue.one_role_or_direction: n/a: no roles or directions; the same encoding rule applies to every construct, and both identifier and literal positions are tested.
wrong_fix_catalogue.reads_only: n/a: no read/write split; this is statement generation, not data access.
wrong_fix_catalogue.check_after_adjustment: n/a: no normalising or adjusting step precedes a sink; the identifier split on dots and the quote-stripping of the existing preparer are exercised only by the coupled functional tests.
wrong_fix_catalogue.malformed_identity: n/a: no parsed identity token; attacker input is a plain name or text value.
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: no authority or secret lookup.

traps.lever: published-fix site (pattern A, reported) plus the shape trap: escaping must neutralise backslash-before-quote and must not destroy legitimate escape sequences
traps.shape: a caller-supplied file name, formatter option value, bucket path, credential, encryption key, stage location, or literal table option is embedded in a single-quoted Snowflake literal; a single quote, or a backslash immediately before one, ends the literal and the rest becomes SQL
traps.reason_to_dismiss: replacing a quote with a backslash-quote, or doubling only the quote, looks like complete escaping; Snowflake's ESCAPE_STRING_LITERALS means a backslash before the quote still escapes it. The opposite mistake (doubling every backslash) breaks the legitimate newline delimiter and the \N null marker.

traps.lever: published-fix far site (pattern A, lower-level public API) with a coupled must-keep-working value
traps.shape: an identifier the caller marked as needing no quotes (the documented no-quote marker) is emitted verbatim in a schema or label position, so a comma, semicolon or comment in the value changes the statement; the same layer must still leave legal bare names bare and must not quote SQLAlchemy's schema-translate placeholder
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the caller explicitly opted out of quoting, so it reads as the caller's responsibility; and the value looks like schema metadata rather than request data. A fix that quotes every marked name breaks the documented bare-name idiom and schema translation.

traps.lever: published-fix far site (pattern A, separate package): a nested selectable compiled by a different compiler than the one embedding it
traps.shape: a value inside a query used as a table option is compiled with the default dialect, so it misses the Snowflake dialect's backslash escaping and a backslash-before-quote ends the literal
traps.reason_to_dismiss: literal binds are already parameterised and a SELECT compiles itself, so the dialect used for the nested compile looks irrelevant

traps.lever: published-fix far site (pattern A, separate package): identifier-valued table options
traps.shape: a warehouse name or a cluster-by expression supplied as text is emitted raw in a CREATE TABLE option
traps.reason_to_dismiss: these options read as application configuration constants, and they live in a separate options package from the command compilers

traps.lever: published-fix far sites (pattern A, the command compilers): names and column keys
traps.shape: MERGE column keys, file-format names (three sinks) and a created stage's name are emitted raw because they look like application-defined identifiers
traps.reason_to_dismiss: column keys are Python keyword arguments and format/stage names are constants declared with the schema, so they read as code rather than data

traps.lever: pattern B route (real, unmodified upstream code the published fix never touches)
traps.shape: a load command's FROM reference is emitted raw for a source table (`.name`) and for a stage's namespace/name, so a reference supplied by the application can carry extra syntax
traps.reason_to_dismiss: a table name is a schema object rather than request data, and an @stage reference reads as a path rather than an identifier position
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code; the published fix quoted only the file_format in the same visitor and left both references alone; current upstream still carries the table `.name` raw

traps.lever: injected sibling: a second stage renderer for the same stage name + storage location operation
traps.shape: ALTER STAGE re-renders the same namespace/name and storage URL as CREATE STAGE, but with the pinned raw f-string and repr(container) shape
traps.reason_to_dismiss: it is a maintenance command rather than the creation path the report names, so fixing the creation renderer looks sufficient
traps.realistic_because: new code in the same style as the adjacent pinned visitor; ALTER STAGE ... SET URL is a real Snowflake statement

traps.lever: injected sibling: a second table-option renderer carrying both an identifier and a literal
traps.shape: a table tag option emits the tag name and its value raw in one clause
traps.reason_to_dismiss: tag names and values are governance metadata supplied from configuration, and the option lives in the options package rather than a compiler
traps.realistic_because: new code in the same style as the existing option classes; Snowflake CREATE TABLE supports a TAG clause
